source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®;
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, nothing being needed by God, and not recognizing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, made in a man in a plague, knowing to bear infirmity, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led like a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and remembering his own dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might rescue them;

pass_b_english: The spiritual disciple truly receives the Spirit of God, who from the beginning attended all God's dispositions toward men, announces what is to come, reveals what is present, and narrates what is past; he judges all, yet is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, consuming their whole activity in vain with a reprobate mind. He judges the Jews also, who do not perceive the word of liberty nor will to go free, though they have a present Liberator; they pretend to serve outside the Law at an unseasonable time, as though God needed anything, and they do not recognize the advent of Christ, which he accomplished for the salvation of men, nor are they willing to understand, since all the prophets announced his two advents: one, in which he was made man in affliction, knowing how to bear weakness, and sat upon a foal of a donkey, and was the stone rejected by the builders, and was led like a sheep to slaughter, and broke Amalech by the extension of his hands; the other, in which he gathers the scattered sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, remembers his own dead who had fallen asleep, and descends to them, so that he might rescue them.

review.notes: Pass B introduces a structural division not present in the Latin source. The Latin text describes the two advents as a single continuous list of attributes/actions following the colon (': unum quidem... congregans autem...), whereas Pass B explicitly adds 'the other, in which' to separate the second half of the sentence. This adds a structural distinction/clause not found in the source. Additionally, Pass B translates 'in homo in plaga factus est' as 'he was made man in affliction', whereas the Latin 'in plaga' (in a plague/blow/affliction) is more specifically rendered in Pass A as 'in a man in a plague', and Pass B's 'made man' is a slight interpretive shift from 'factus est' in this context.
reasons: Pass B adds 'the other, in which' to separate the second part of the list, which is not in the Latin source: '...prophetee: unum quidem... congregans autem...'
